# FDG8102

> DO implement `IEquatable<T>`, with the same behavior as the operator, on any type that defines `operator==`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.13 Equality Operators.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG8102
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

Message: Type '{0}' defines operator == but does not implement IEquatable<{0}>

FDG8102 reports the first operator == declared in a class or struct that does not implement IEquatable<T> of itself. Whether IEquatable<T>.Equals behaves like the operator is not checked, so coverage is partial. Adding the interface adds to the public API without changing a signature; there is no code fix.

## From the book

For more information on `IEquatable<T>`, see section 8.6.
